summary: Registered the third lead and requested its probe. The question: can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx, with the documented Superseded heuristic shadowed because drain_notifiers matches the index-based arm first. The probe (draft identity_probe.rs, omnipaxos_runtime package) is locally verified and deterministic: node 1 is isolated in both directions and accepts its own entry 42 at index 1 (never replicated, read back as Undecided); node 2 takes over with an empty log and decides index 1 with its own entry 99; node 1 is re-admitted via its normal Promise + AcceptSync re-synchronization, which truncates its log to node 2's and raises its decided index to 1. Local run emits after_b_takeover {b_leader:(2,true), c_leader:(2,true), a_leader:(1,true), b_decided:0, c_decided:0} and overwritten_index_resolution {a_decided_idx:1, a_entry_at_index_1_is_own:false, b_decided_idx:1, b_idx:1, resolution:"Ok(1)"} — the call reports success at the index that another entry occupies. Two harness bugs were found and fixed on the way: the manual transport needed a delivery task (nothing was pumped while awaiting a handle call, which had made node 2's own append_notify time out), and the isolation must cover both directions and start before the append, otherwise node 1's entry leaks out and is legitimately adopted. Also added the Superseded doc as a source. The receipt will follow next turn; no execution result is claimed yet.
